title: Onboarding Samples & Runtime Accelerator for SDKs
author: Samira Patel
content:
OVERVIEW

Short intro: This page centralizes the "Runtime Accelerator" sample library and onboarding playbook for SDK authors and integrators. It bundles compact, runnable examples (embed-first, generation-first, streaming, and hybrid), publishing and review controls for docs site owners, and a canonical triage map for the top 8 support issues encountered during early SDK adoption.

GOALS
- Reduce time-to-first-success for engineers integrating Redwood SDKs from days to under 2 hours.
- Provide deterministic examples that exercise production runtime features: batching, streaming, KV cache reuse, and error-handling.
- Standardize doc publishing and golden-trace validation so examples stay runnable across runtime releases.

AUDIENCE
- SDK engineers (maintainers and contributors)
- Developer advocates and DX writers
- Solutions engineers onboarding customers

SCOPE & COMPONENTS
1) Sample Library (runnable artifacts)
   - sample-embed-pipeline: small Go + Py examples showing embedding batching and sparse caching.
   - sample-gen-stream: Node + Python streaming example with reconnection and resume tokens.
   - sample-hybrid-search-gen: full end-to-end sample combining embeddings -> reranker -> generator.
2) Quickstart playbooks (this doc)
3) Validation harness: golden traces and CI job definitions (docs-ci/golden-trace-runner)
4) Support canonical fixes mapping

HOW TO USE (QUICKSTARTS)
- Quickstart: minimal generator (Python)
  1. pip install redwood-sdk==2.1.0
  2. export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REDACTED
  3. python -c "from redwood import Client; c=Client(); print(c.generate('Write a haiku about caching'))"

- Streaming reconnect snippet (Node)
  - key steps:
    1) subscribe to event stream
    2) buffer partial chunks with idempotency token
    3) on disconnect, resume using stream_resume_token
  - sample snippet:
    const c = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
    const res = await c.streamGenerate({ prompt: 'Explain prefix caching', stream: true, resumeToken: lastToken });

PUBLISHING WORKFLOW FOR SAMPLES (docs-site owners)
1. Author creates PR against docs repo and attaches: sample code, Dockerfile (if applicable), and a small smoke test (run-local.sh).
2. CI runs: unit tests, golden-trace runner, and container build smoke.
3. Reviewer (DX writer + SDK maintainer) signs off. Required labels: docs-sample, smoke-tested.
4. Merge window: weekday 09:00–17:00 UTC; if merging outside window, notify #devx-channel.
5. Post-merge: automated job deploys sample to staging and validates canonical traces for latest runtime tag.

GOLDEN TRACE CONTRACTS
| sample | inputs | stable fields | acceptable delta |
| sample-gen-stream | prompt sized 8–128 tokens | token-sequence, complete flag | +/- 2 tokens on final chunk |
| sample-embed-pipeline | 10 short docs | embedding L2-norm | < 0.05 change per model minor bump |

DOCS SLOs & OWNER METRICS
- Example run success rate >= 98% in staging (CI-run) per release.
- Sample smoke time < 90s on standard CI runner (2 vCPU, 8GB RAM).
- Ownership: docs-site engineering (primary), eng-devx (secondary). Contact: samira.patel@redwood.ai

CANONICAL SUPPORT ISSUE MAP (Top 8) — triage + fix
1) Symptom: SDK install fails on Python 3.11 with wheel errors.
   - Cause: missing manylinux wheel for new build; CI omitted universal wheel step.
   - Fix: Add manylinux2014 wheel build target; publish artifact and bump docs with compatibility note.
2) Symptom: Streaming reconnect resumes duplicate tokens.
   - Cause: server-side resume idempotency token mismatch when client retries without checkpointing.
   - Fix: Example updated to persist last_resume_token and deduplicate partial buffers in client.
3) Symptom: Embeddings drift after quantized model upgrade.
   - Cause: incompatible quantization profile in runtime-config.
   - Fix: Add a compatibility shim and note to release notes + recommended profile mapping table.
(remaining items summarized for brevity in doc; full canonical-fixes list maintained in repo under /support/canonical-fixes)

RELEASE-CONTROLLED CONFIG SNIPPET
{
  "sample_ci": "golden-trace-runner: v1",
  "runtime_profile": "embeddings-stable-v2",
  "smoke_timeout": "90s",
  "maintainers": "eng-devx"
}

LOCAL DEBUG & EMULATION
- To run locally: repo contains run-local.sh, which launches a lightweight emulation container (uses runtime-stub:0.3). Example:
  ./run-local.sh sample-gen-stream --env-file .env.local
- Telemetry: enable DEBUG_SAMPLE=1 to surface per-sample telemetry to stdout; do not commit local .env files.

ESCALATION FOR UNRESOLVED SAMPLE FAILURES
1. If CI golden-trace failure persists for > 3 consecutive runs, create a ticket in the docs-support queue and @mention SDK oncall.
2. Attach CI logs, sample id, runtime tag, and the failing golden trace.
3. Oncall process:
   a. confirm whether change originated in runtime or docs.
   b. if runtime: open incident runbook and follow runtime rollback steps.
   c. if docs: revert the sample or patch immediately with smoke test.

MAINTENANCE & ROTATION
- Owners must review each sample on major runtime release or every 6 months, whichever comes first.
- Deprecated samples: add label deprecated-sample and move code to /archive with README describing reason.

RELATED LINKS
- SDK repo: https://git.redwood.ai/sdk
- Golden-trace runner: https://git.redwood.ai/docs-ci/golden-trace-runner
- Support canonical fixes: https://git.redwood.ai/support/canonical-fixes

APPENDIX: CHECKLIST FOR NEW SAMPLE SUBMISSION
1. runnable in CI with a 90s smoke test
2. contains README with expected outputs and golden trace
3. has small deterministic input set
4. includes owner and maintainer contact
5. labeled and linked in this doc

End of doc.
